text: The Getty Center, located in the Brentwood neighborhood of Los Angeles, California, US, is a campus of the J. Paul Getty Museum and other programs of the Getty Trust. It opened to the public on December 16, 1997, and is renowned for its architecture, gardens, and panoramic views of Los Angeles, the San Bernardino Mountains, the San Gabriel Mountains, and the Pacific Ocean. Situated atop a 900-foot (270-meter) hill in a 24-acre (9.7 ha) area on a 110-acre (45 ha) site within the Santa Monica Mountains above Interstate 405, the center is connected to a visitors' parking garage at the base by an automated three-car, cable-pulled hovertrain people mover. The center draws 1.8 million visitors annually and features pre-20th-century European paintings, drawings, illuminated manuscripts, sculpture, decorative arts, and photographs from the 1830s to the present day from around the world, including a collection displayed in the lower level of the west pavilion. The museum also includes outdoor sculpture on terraces and in gardens, with the 134,000-square-foot (12,400 m²) Central Garden designed by Robert Irwin, completed in December 1997, and a "Lower Terrace Garden" added in 2007. The campus is designed by architect Richard Meier, who used two grids offset at a 22.5-degree angle to define space, with one axis housing galleries and the other housing administrative buildings, and emphasized strong visual lines throughout. The buildings are constructed from concrete and steel with travertine or aluminum cladding, using approximately 1,200,000 square feet (110,000 m²) of travertine. The site includes a seven-story underground parking garage with over 1,200 spaces and a cost-based parking system. The center houses the Getty Research Institute (GRI), the Getty Conservation Institute (GCI), the Getty Foundation, and the J. Paul Getty Trust. The GRI, located to the west of the museum, contains over 900,000 volumes, two million photographs, and offers public exhibitions, publications, and a scholars program. The GCI, which began operations in 1985, focuses on scientific research, education, and conservation in both art and architecture. The Getty Foundation awards grants for the understanding and preservation of the visual arts and runs the Getty Leadership Institute. The buildings are designed with robust earthquake and fire safety features, including retrofitted steelwork after the 1994 Northridge earthquake, and fire-resistant materials such as travertine, protected steel, and crushed stone roofs, with fire-resistant landscaping, pruned oak trees, and a 1,000,000 US gal (3,800,000 L) water tank at the north end. The interior includes fire-protected walls, automatic fire doors, pressurized air systems, and silicone-cooled transformers. In 2017, the Skirball Fire was stopped by damp earth from the center’s irrigation system, and in January 2025, the Getty Center was placed in a mandatory evacuation zone due to the Palisades Fire. The total project cost was $1.3 billion, with $733 million allocated for construction, land and site work, fixtures and equipment, and insurance, engineering, and permits. The land and buildings were estimated at $3.853 billion in June 2013. The museum's permanent collection is displayed chronologically across five pavilions, with the north housing the oldest art and the west housing the newest, and the exhibitions pavilion serving as a temporary space. The rotunda building includes information desks, orientation theatres, museum shops, a grand staircase, and a terrace linking all five pavilions. The center's administrative buildings, including the auditorium, North Building, and East Building, are closed to the public except for special events. The museum also offers exhibitions, family workshops, school visits, performances, talks, and tours. Originally established in 1954 in J. Paul Getty's Pacific Palisades home, the collection expanded into a replica Italian villa opened in 1974, which was later renamed the Getty Villa and closed for renovations in 2006 to focus on ancient Greek, Roman, and Etruscan art. The Getty Trust faced financial difficulties in 2008 and 2009, cutting 205 staff positions and reducing its endowment from $6.4 billion in 2007 to $4.5 billion in 2009, before recovering to $6.2 billion by 2013. In 2005, after a Los Angeles Times investigation, the California Attorney General found no violations, and the trust agreed to appoint an outside monitor. The center's design includes a seven-story underground parking garage, access roads, staff parking, and a hillside planted with California Live Oak trees. The main axes of the grid begin at the arrival plaza and extend through the rotunda, columns, and courtyard, with cross axes linking the GRI library garden to the rotunda. Portions of the exhibitions pavilion and east pavilion are aligned on the true north–south axis to emphasize the dual grids. The museum's interior features computer-controlled skylights for paintings and light-sensitive art on the first floor, while second-floor galleries are connected by glass bridges and terraces. Fountains provide background white noise, with benches and fences installed to prevent wading, and modifications made to comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act. The north promontory includes a heliport, and the south promontory features a cactus garden. The complex is linked by landscaped terraces and an enclosed glass walkway from the rotunda.

Electrical transformers at the center of the facility use silicone fluid as a coolant, which poses less risk of ignition compared to hydrocarbon coolants. The sprinkler system, intended as a last resort, is designed to balance the potential damage from a fire against the risk of water damage to valuable artwork. In 2017, the Skirball Fire nearly spread to the Getty Center on December 6, when an ember drifted over to the Getty hill; the damp earth, soaked with 1.2 million gallons of water from the Getty's irrigation pipes, prevented the fire from spreading, and the fire department extinguished it without further damage. During the January 2025 Southern California wildfires, the Getty Center was placed in the mandatory evacuation zone due to the spread of the Palisades Fire.
